html:
Tutankhamun was a pharaoh of Egypt's Eighteenth Dynasty who came to the throne as a boy around 1332 BCE and died at about 19, around 1323 BCE. He was a minor king in his own time but is the most famous pharaoh today, because his tomb was found almost untouched.

He was born Tutankhaten, probably the son of Akhenaten, the king who had pushed aside Egypt's many gods in favour of the sun disc, the Aten, in the movement called Atenism. Akhenaten's queen was Nefertiti. Under Tutankhamun, or rather his advisers, the old religion came back. The court left Akhenaten's new city of Amarna, the temples of Amun were reopened, and the king changed his name to Tutankhamun, "living image of Amun".

He died young; the cause is still unknown. Scans of his mummy show a broken leg and signs of malaria, but neither is proven to have killed him. Later kings, beginning with Horemheb, struck him and the other Amarna kings from the official lists.

Being forgotten saved his tomb. It was small and later buried under rubble from other tombs in the Valley of the Kings, so robbers mostly missed it. In November 1922 the archaeologist Howard Carter found it, packed with more than five thousand objects: gilded shrines, chariots, jewellery and the solid gold mask of the king.

The find caused a craze for ancient Egypt around the world, and stories of a "curse" spread when Carter's patron died a few months later. It remains the best picture we have of the wealth of New Kingdom Egypt.
